symptom.disease_name: Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

sampled_features.disease_name: Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

additional_requirements: delusions_and_hallucinations occur exclusively during the manic episode

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

S033.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
S033.description: A distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood.

subtypes.Elevated Mood: A mood that is abnormally high, euphoric, and full of unmotivated happiness and vitality.
subtypes.Irritable Mood: A state where one gets angry or aggressive even at minor stimuli.
subtypes.Mood Lability: Rapid shifts in mood, alternating unpredictably between euphoria and irritability.

S034.name: Increased_Activity
S034.description: Abnormally and persistently increased goal-directed activity or energy.

subtypes.Increased Energy: Overflowing physical and mental energy, leading to an inability to stay still and a desire to keep moving.
subtypes.Hyperactivity: Doing far more work than usual or starting multiple activities simultaneously.
subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Inability to tolerate resting or stopping, driven by a constant need to do something.

S035.name: Inflated_Self_Esteem
S035.description: Inflated self-esteem or grandiosity (may range from uncritical self-confidence to delusional proportions).

subtypes.Inflated Self-Confidence: Feeling capable of anything and believing that failure is impossible, unlike one's usual self.
subtypes.Overestimation of Abilities: Unrealistically assessing one's talents, knowledge, or abilities as superior.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one is a special and important person with a special mission or purpose.

S037.name: Pressured_Speech
S037.description: More talkative than usual or pressure to keep talking.

subtypes.Talkativeness: Speaking far more than usual and continuing to talk without rest.
subtypes.Rapid Speech: Speech speed is so fast that it is difficult for others to understand or interrupt.
subtypes.Pressured Speech: Cannot stop talking or tolerate silence due to an internal pressure to keep speaking.

S039.name: Manic_Distractibility
S039.description: Attention is too easily drawn to unimportant or irrelevant external stimuli.

subtypes.Responsiveness to Extraneous Stimuli: Attention is immediately drawn to trivial and unimportant stimuli nearby (e.g., noise, movement).
subtypes.Frequent Task Switching: Unable to finish one task and constantly shifting attention to new things, starting multiple tasks simultaneously.
subtypes.Inability to Sustain Attention: Unable to focus on any activity for long, with attention constantly being scattered.

S040.name: Increased_Goal_Activity
S040.description: Increase in goal-directed activity (at work, school, socially, or sexually) or purposeless psychomotor agitation.

subtypes.Occupational Hyperactivity: Driving significantly more projects or work than usual in the workplace or academic setting.
subtypes.Social Hyperactivity: Becoming much more sociable and extroverted than usual, actively meeting and contacting people.
subtypes.Hypersexuality: Significantly increased interest in or activity regarding sex.
subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Purposeless non-goal-directed activity, such as pacing or hand-wringing, driven by an inability to sit still.

S041.name: Painful_Consequence_Behavior
S041.description: Excessive involvement in activities that have a high potential for painful consequences.

subtypes.Unrestrained Buying Sprees: Spending excessive amounts of money or shopping recklessly to a degree that creates financial distress for self and family.
subtypes.Foolish Business Investments: Making rash business investments or ventures without sufficient review.
subtypes.Sexual Indiscretions: Engaging in indiscriminate or risky sexual behavior that is out of character.
subtypes.Impulsive Risky Behavior: Excessively dangerous or foolish behavior, such as reckless driving or drug use, without considering the consequences.

symptom.disease_info: Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features is characterized by at least one fully syndromal manic episode lasting at least a week (or requiring hospitalization), often with marked impairment in social or occupational functioning. During severe manic episodes, mood-congruent or mood-incongruent psychotic features such as delusions or hallucinations can emerge, typically resolving as the mood episode remits. The course is usually recurrent, with episodes of mania and often depression separated by periods of relative euthymia, though some individuals have rapid cycling or chronic symptoms. It is distinguished from schizoaffective and primary psychotic disorders by the temporal relationship between psychosis and mood episodes and by the presence of clear-cut manic symptomatology.

patient.stressor: Dolores entered a particularly unstable period in her freelance work when two longstanding illustration contracts ended unexpectedly and an anticipated adjunct course was cancelled for low enrollment. Already prone to overcommitment, she reacted by saying yes to every new project offer, expanding her workload beyond what she could realistically manage, while also worrying about her irregular income and overdue taxes. Over the next three months, her previously comforting routines around gardening, walking, and museum visits were increasingly displaced by frantic efforts to "fix" her financial situation through ambitious new commissions and speculative proposals, straining her organization and leading to late payments and confused interactions with clients. Her sister and a close neighbor encouraged her to seek help after they noticed she was talking rapidly about improbable financial opportunities, neglecting basic paperwork, and insisting she had discovered a "sure way" to secure her retirement, prompting her to present for psychiatric care when she realized her money management and work commitments were spiraling out of control.
patient.chief_complaint: “I keep taking on more and more projects and plans at once, and I can’t seem to slow myself down even though everything in my life is starting to fall apart.”

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.
S019.manifestation: Lately I’ve been completely convinced that the IRS and one of my old clients are quietly coordinating to sabotage me—like the delayed payments, the lost checks, even the audit notice are all part of a plan to push me into bankruptcy because they know I’m onto some big, valuable ideas, and no matter what my sister says I can’t shake the feeling that it’s intentional, not coincidence or clerical error.

S033.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
S033.description: A distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood.
S033.manifestation: Most days I’m either buzzing with this almost giddy excitement about all my “brilliant” projects or snapping at people for the smallest interruption—like I’ll be raving to my neighbor about how I’m going to triple my income, and then if she asks a simple question I’ll suddenly feel enraged, like she’s trying to block me or slow me down.

S034.name: Increased_Activity
S034.description: Abnormally and persistently increased goal-directed activity or energy.
S034.manifestation: I wake up before dawn already pacing around the apartment, jumping from my desk to the kitchen to my studio corner, sketching, answering emails, reorganizing files, and I just can’t sit still long enough to finish any one thing before I’m compelled to start three more.

S035.name: Inflated_Self_Esteem
S035.description: Inflated self-esteem or grandiosity (may range from uncritical self-confidence to delusional proportions).
S035.manifestation: I keep telling my sister that I’m finally operating at the level I was meant to, that I can single-handedly revive my whole career and even “redefine illustration education” with these workshops I’m planning, and I honestly feel baffled and a little insulted when she suggests I might be overestimating what one person can do.

S037.name: Pressured_Speech
S037.description: More talkative than usual or pressure to keep talking.
S037.manifestation: When I get going about my new commissions and this “retirement plan” I’ve cooked up, I talk so fast and jump from idea to idea that people have to interrupt me to ask me to slow down, but I feel this pressure in my chest to keep explaining before the thoughts slip away, so it’s really hard to stop or let anyone else get a word in.

S039.name: Manic_Distractibility
S039.description: Attention is too easily drawn to unimportant or irrelevant external stimuli.
S039.manifestation: I’ll sit down to invoice a client and then the ping of an email, a bird outside, or even a color in a magazine will pull me off into another direction—suddenly I’m redesigning my website, then sketching a new series, then reorganizing my brushes, and an hour later I realize I never finished the invoice I started.

S040.name: Increased_Goal_Activity
S040.description: Increase in goal-directed activity (at work, school, socially, or sexually) or purposeless psychomotor agitation.
S040.manifestation: I’ve been saying yes to every commission, pitching new series to galleries, drafting online course outlines, and even sketching a children’s book all at once, to the point where my calendar is a wall of overlapping deadlines and I’m constantly juggling late nights and frantic emails just to keep anything from completely collapsing.

S041.name: Painful_Consequence_Behavior
S041.description: Excessive involvement in activities that have a high potential for painful consequences.
S041.manifestation: I’ve started putting big expenses on my nearly maxed-out credit cards for supplies and “investments” in my brand, and I even put down a nonrefundable deposit on a pricey studio space I can’t really afford because I was so sure these grand plans would pay off, even though a more rational part of me knows I’m gambling with money I don’t have.
